changes.ink: The first digit has two open rounded lobes; the second has an ascending upper stroke returning into a closed lower loop. The lighter 36 is in an unassigned hand.
The looped l and low e, followed by the c opening and joined arr/e strokes, are readable; the final raised terminal stroke belongs to the accented ending.

A crossed stacked group precedes the live xi/eta fraction. The upper angular and lower descending shapes support the tentative fraction, but their crossings obscure parts; no certainty is supplied. H only comments on overtracing and omits this cancelled group.
After the compact a-like mark, the abbreviation has a dotted i, low s, rounded o, and point; there is no second e of i.e.

The word begins with low undulating strokes, unlike the long p descender in the following près. Its horizontal stroke is below all the letter bodies, like the underline under unique; it is not a secure through-letter cancellation. An unfinished un-like beginning or aux remains possible.
The low u/n/i strokes lead to a looped q with a long descender and the final u/e. A separate line runs below the word. There is no long isomorphismes sequence.
A compact à precedes the low m/e and tall crossed t strokes of mettre; the initial i/m/p sequence of imposée is absent.
One detached upright follows lambda. The next thin upright is attached to the small annotation cluster over the equals sign, not a second independent prime.

The small looped d/f-like cluster lies above the two short horizontal equality strokes. A descending stroke from the preceding text crosses the area, so the exact df reading remains doubtful. C puts the annotation below the sign and H omits it.
Despite retouching, the curved upper entry, descending diagonal and broad returning lower foot give 2. The crossing remains an overtrace; no earlier numeral is invented.
The final 2 has a returning foot and blank space to its right; no separate final point appears.
A tall crossed t is followed by the low ermes sequence. There is no initial descending p or the later -nant sequence of prenant.
A small ascending stroke and low body survive before e1 under a heavy horizontal strike. They support de only tentatively; the strike prevents complete letter recovery.
The superscript consists of the angled upper part, cross stroke and descending limb of 4. There is no separate circled cross before it.
After the looped initial d, a long low connected onnan sequence ends in a short t. Une is separate; no extra aussi word is present.

Par sits at the start of the main formula baseline. Above xi0, eta0 a leader joins the interlinear la paire d’éléments distincts: the p descender and the short aire ending distinguish paire from couple. No original parenthesis precedes that leader.
The low initial ou and the separate encore have the rounded c and linked ending; there is no dotted i.e. followed by aussi.
The membership sign and C stand above the mu/xi0/eta0 baseline. A long curved leader returns from their right to the insertion place after eta0. Both witnesses flatten this raised addition.
A short detached curved stroke descends at the baseline after eta0, to the right of the returning insertion leader. Its separation from the long leader supports a comma before satisfaisant.
The word has an accented e, the c opening, a descending p, and the joined -érant ending. The surrounding se and comme are distinct.

A long line lies below the complete comparison, with an extended upward left end and a small upward right end. A separate tall vertical stroke stands just to the right, before s’exprime. Both line strokes are reproduced without assigning a punctuation role. The raised black cluster after the second mu remains doubtful, possibly a cancelled 2; the drawing does not resolve it.
The initial s/apostrophe is followed by the x crossing and long p descender of exprime, then the separate par. No signifiant que sequence is written.
The short form starts néc with an accent and ends in a raised t. The following two words are non nulles; car begins the next baseline before leur produit est 1. H omits the nonzero wording.
After the round O/n, the word shows the low récu sequence, a descending p and the final ère. It is live after the cancelled word.
The words follow comme on the same ascending baseline as solutions de. There is no insertion leader or separate higher line, and no point after ens.

notes.text: This portrait handwritten page is on the reverse of listing paper. The pale blue mechanically printed matter is laterally reversed and is excluded as show-through; C mistakenly treated it as additional front text. The lighter top-left 36 is retained as unassigned foliation. No authorial number or date is inferred from H’s editorial notes.

The opening continues a preceding discussion. It writes lambda as a ratio involving xi wedge eta and as xi/eta+eta/xi+2, then shifts to lambda-prime=lambda−2. The geometric identification, the wedge/product convention and the claimed recovery up to unique isomorphism were not independently proved from this isolated leaf.

The page writes e1^4=e=xi wedge eta, uses e1^2 as a base of L2, and introduces distinct scalar coordinates xi0,eta0 with product1 and sum mu. These conventions are transcribed; no tensor symbol is added before the fourth-power exponent.

For the scalar quadratic z^2−mu z+1, the computed discriminant is mu^2−4. Over C, nonzero discriminant gives two distinct roots; their product1 makes both nonzero. Thus the condition is mu≠±2. If the raised dark mark in the manuscript’s second comparison is a live2, that written comparison would be a slip: mu=2 would satisfy mu^2≠±2 while giving the repeated root1. The ink remains unresolved.

Expanding (z^2−xi0)(z^2−eta0) and substituting xi0+eta0=mu and xi0 eta0=1 gives z^4−mu z^2+1. Each nonzero scalar root has two opposite square roots over C, and distinct scalar roots give disjoint pairs, yielding four distinct roots under the stated discriminant condition.

The radical expression follows by solving the quadratic in z^2. The rescaling mu-prime=mu/2 converts (mu^2−4)/4 to mu-prime^2−1; the two inner sign choices give the same set after this rescaling. A closing parenthesis and final punctuation not readable at the clipped paper edge are not silently supplied.

The short word following iso. is underlined but remains unclear, tentatively un|aux. Its strokes differ from the clear later près. The cancelled fraction, de and Les retain their doubts; the superscript after mu is not forced by the discriminant calculation.

checks.outcome: Each nonzero a in C has exactly two distinct roots of z^2=a. If a and b are distinct, a root cannot satisfy both equations. Therefore the two distinct nonzero quadratic roots produce four distinct quartic roots.
